title: Reservation Scheduling Transparency & Rollback PRD
creator: Asha Patel
description: Deliver a reservation scheduling transparency layer and a safe rollback mechanism for reserved pool changes. This PRD defines customer-visible timelines, API surfaces, console views, audit trails, and rollback workflows so tenants and platform operators can see scheduled reserve shifts and safely revert or stage changes when required.
goals: Provide a clear reserved-pool schedule view in Console and API with timelines, upcoming changes, and effective windows.
Implement a queriable audit trail for reserve modifications (who, what, when) with immutability for 90 days.
Add a tested rollback flow that can revert a reservation change within a defined rollback window without manual infra restore.
Expose alerting hooks and telemetry so SRE and tenant admins can be notified of upcoming effective changes and successful rollbacks.
non_goals: Building a full chargeback billing engine (only emit events for billing systems).
Changing the underlying autoscaler scheduling algorithm -- we will surface decisions but not replace scheduler logic in this ticket.
Implementing tenant-specific custom policies beyond a default configurable rollback window (future work).
user_personas: Tenant Admin (product/customer): needs transparency about when reserved capacity changes take effect and the ability to request reversions.
Platform Engineer: needs instrumentation and safe operator rollback without disrupting other tenants.
Oncall SRE: needs alerts, runbook links, and playbook steps when reserve changes cause issues.
user_stories: As a Tenant Admin, I want to see a timeline of upcoming reservation changes and the exact time they will take effect so I can plan deployments.
As a Platform Engineer, I want to trigger a safe rollback of a recent reserve reallocation within 30 minutes of a change to recover SLA violations.
As an Oncall SRE, I want to receive alerts when a scheduled reservation change increases preemption risk so I can prepare mitigation steps.
functional_requirements: API: GET /v1/reservations/:id returns current state, pending changes, effective_time, requester, and reason.
API: POST /v1/reservations/:id/rollback creates a rollback request that is validated and queued; only available during rollback_window.
Console: Reservation timeline UI on Dedicated > Reservations with clear color coding for pending/effective/rolled-back states and an action 'Request rollback' for eligible reservations.
Audit trail: Immutable log entries for reservation create/update/delete/rollback with actor, timestamp, delta, and linked ticket IDs, retained 90 days.
Telemetry: Emit events to telemetry bus for change_scheduled, change_applied, rollback_requested, rollback_completed with reservation_id and tenant_id tags.
Access controls: Only tenant admins (owner role) and platform SRE (operator role) can request rollback; role checks must reuse existing RBAC service.
Rollback semantics: rollback should attempt best-effort to restore previous reservation sizing and placement; if partial restore required, return structured failure reason and remediation steps.
Safeguards: Rollback API must be idempotent within the window and must surface conflict errors when another change intervened.
nonfunctional_requirements: API responses for reservation endpoints must be <200ms 95th percentile under normal control-plane load.
Audit events must be written to immutable store with write latency <500ms and durability SLA matching existing control-plane logs.
Rollback end-to-end should complete within 5 minutes for >90% of requests, or else surface a long-running job with progress.
All surfaces must comply with existing KMS/KMS-backed audit encryption policies and require security_review_required before GA.
Feature flags must gate rollout per-tenant and allow quick disable.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a reservation timeline for a reservation with at least a pending change, with correct effective_time and color states in Chrome and Firefox.
GET /v1/reservations/:id returns a JSON payload documenting pending_changes array with effective_time and rationale; response schema validated by integration tests.
POST /v1/reservations/:id/rollback returns 202 when accepted and creates a rollback job, and subsequent telemetry events rollback_requested and rollback_completed are emitted.
RBAC: Non-authorized users attempting rollback receive 403, authorized users succeed per tests tied to RBAC harness.
Audit logs contain immutable entries for schedule create and schedule rollback with actor and original delta; log entries retrievable via /v1/audit?reservation_id=... for at least 90 days.

Rollback flow tested in staging with tenants using reserved pools and validated to restore previous allocation in >= 90% of synthetic scenarios; edge cases produce documented failure codes and remediation guidance.
Alerts fire to SRE Slack channel when a scheduled change has preemption risk score > 70 and at least one alert runbook link is included.
dependencies: ENG-42011 (scheduler: expose preemption risk score API)
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only flag for 2 tenants + platform SRE testing (2 weeks).
Beta: 10 pilot tenants opt-in via console toggle + monitor metrics (4 weeks).
GA: global rollout with default 30-minute rollback window and documented runbook (post successful beta metrics).
Rollback window configurable per-tenant but behind feature flag for incremental enablement.
metrics_and_kpis: Time-to-visibility: time between schedule creation and visibility in Console (target < 5s).
Rollback success rate: percentage of rollback requests that fully restore prior allocation (target >= 90%).
Average rollback time: median end-to-end time (target < 5 minutes).
Audit retrieval success: percent of audit queries returning entries (target >= 99%).
Number of post-change incidents traced to scheduled reservation changes (target: reduce by 50% compared to baseline).
open_questions: What is the default rollback window? Proposal: 30 minutes. PM feedback: allow tenants to request 15/30/60 minute presets behind flag.
If partial restore is required (insufficient capacity), should we automatically queue a backfill or surface to tenant to negotiate a grace? Decision pending.
Do we need explicit tenant opt-in for emitting reservation telemetry to external billing systems? Legal/compliance to advise.
decisions: Use existing RBAC service for permission checks rather than add new role layer.
Retention: audit entries retained for 90 days in immutable store (complies with platform logging policy).
Expose rollback as a queued job to avoid blocking control-plane synchronous operations.
notes: Scope clarification (2026-03-05): this ticket will not change underlying scheduler placement; it surfaces and orchestrates rollback requests against the current scheduler API.
Scope change (2026-03-09): added telemetry event rollback_requested and rollback_completed after engineering feasibility spike.
Design note: timeline UI will reuse existing timeline component but add a new legend and compact mode for mobile.
